title: High fructose corn syrup: what it means for your plan
standfirst: Which of our plan rules this ingredient turns on, and what that does not tell you.

spans.text: High-fructose corn syrup: a liquid sweetener made from cornstarch that is enzymatically processed to convert some glucose into fructose.
Why it is in your food
Manufacturers use high fructose corn syrup as a sweetener/sugar and it is of plant origin.
Our rules read high fructose corn syrup as a refined syrup.

Our scorer looks for high fructose corn syrup when Autoimmune Protocol (AIP), Diabetes, Gout, Low-FODMAP or Fatty liver (NAFLD) is on for you. If those plans are off, your score does not change. This is how the app reads a label. It is not a claim about health.
Labels do not all use the same word for this. Below is every spelling we watch for. Some come from other languages, because a pack made for another country prints its own.

items: jarabe de maiz de alta fructosa

spans.text: One word on a label can cover more than one thing. A plan may also turn on how much is in the food, which this page cannot see. Read the pack when it matters.
